recommended_project_title: MineShark: Tor encrypted anonymous-traffic risk analysis and LLM-assisted triage
selection_rule: Prefer Tor traffic datasets that are used, released, or directly constructed by Tor / website-fingerprinting papers from USENIX Security, IEEE S&P, ACM CCS, and NDSS in the most recent three-year window.

datasets.paper_or_artifact: Rimmer-style AWF Tor website-fingerprinting traces reused by recent WF work
datasets.notes: Use as the first reproducible Tor WF baseline. Convert packet or cell direction and timestamp sequences to PPI.

datasets.venue: IEEE Symposium on Security and Privacy
datasets.paper_or_artifact: Robust Multi-tab Website Fingerprinting Attacks in the Wild / Multitab-WF-Datasets
datasets.notes: Use for Tor multi-tab traffic behavior, micro/macro F1, and Hamming loss evaluation.

datasets.paper_or_artifact: Realistic Website Fingerprinting by Augmenting Network Traces / NetCLR drift-style traces
datasets.notes: Use to show that Tor traffic models need temporal validation instead of only random splits.

datasets.paper_or_artifact: Transformer-based Model for Multi-tab Website Fingerprinting Attack
datasets.notes: Use as a transformer-oriented Tor WF comparison point when the artifact or derived traces are available.

datasets.paper_or_artifact: Walkie-Talkie defended Tor website-fingerprinting traces reused by robust WF evaluations
datasets.notes: Use to report how the detector behaves on defended or padded Tor traces.

datasets.paper_or_artifact: Stop, Don't Click Here Anymore: Boosting Website Fingerprinting by Considering Sets of Subpages
datasets.notes: Use as a methodology reference for collecting Tor subpage traces if the released dataset is unavailable.

datasets.paper_or_artifact: On Precisely Detecting Censorship Circumvention in Real-World Networks
datasets.notes: Use as a methodology and FPR caution for Tor-related detection. It is not the first dataset to implement unless an accessible artifact is available.
Use only as external realism evidence because it is not a primary four-top-conference dataset.
